title: From Attention to 3-Bit Caches: How LLMs Learned to Remember Less (MHA, GQA, MLA, MoE, Quantisation Explained)
why_read: An accessible, well-structured explainer tying together a whole lineage of LLM efficiency techniques in one narrative.
analysis: This post walks through the practical engineering tricks that made large language models usable at scale after the original Transformer paper, including KV caching, grouped-query and multi-head latent attention, FlashAttention, mixture of experts, and quantization. These are genuinely important techniques that determine how much memory and compute a model needs to serve, directly affecting cost and latency in production systems. The writing style is casual and uses analogies to stay approachable without requiring a research background, which makes it a good primer rather than a novel contribution. Good for engineers who want a conceptual map of why modern LLM serving looks the way it does, even if it offers nothing new to specialists.
